record.paper_title: Exactly unsolved problems of interacting 1D fermions
record.context_brief: Bethe-ansatz excitations and scattering in the s-d exchange tunneling model
record.original_question: In the one-dimensional s-d exchange tunneling model for two metal leads, two effective Dirac-electron species represent the two leads, a chemical-potential bias distinguishes the species, and weak tunneling occurs at a point through an impurity spin with exchange couplings. For this two-channel Kondo-type problem, what are the physical Bethe-ansatz quasiparticle excitations, and what are the bulk and impurity scattering matrices for those excitations?

evidence.quote: In this section we describe two 1D models of electrons tunneling through a point-like defect either by the s-d exchange (Kondo) mechanism, or via the resonanse level (Anderson) mechanism. These models are potential candidates to be solved exactly in the presence of arbitrary external bias by means of the Bethe-ansatz technique.

The same "unfolding" procedure can be applied to the left piece of metal to map the problem eventually to the full axis. We end up with two species of free Dirac electrons on the line, to which we assign the flavor index m = 1, 2.
To summurize, the questions to be answered are: what are the physical excitations in the Bethe ansatz solution of (5)-(7) and their scattering matrices?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a one-dimensional model of two metallic leads coupled at a single point through an impurity spin via an s–d (Kondo) exchange interaction. After linearizing the dispersion near the Fermi points and unfolding each semi-infinite lead onto the full real line, the low-energy degrees of freedom in each lead m ∈ {1,2} are two species of right-moving Dirac fermions ψ_{m,σ}(x), σ ∈ {↑,↓}, with Hamiltonian density

  H_0 = −i Σ_{m,σ} ψ†_{m,σ}(x) ∂_x ψ_{m,σ}(x),

together with a chemical-potential bias term

  H_bias = Σ_{m,σ} μ_m ψ†_{m,σ}(x) ψ_{m,σ}(x),  μ_1 − μ_2 = V,

and a point-like impurity exchange at x = 0,

  H_imp = Σ_{m,m'} Σ_{a∈{x,y,z}} J^a_{m m'} ψ†_{m,α}(0) (σ^a/2)_{αβ} ψ_{m',β}(0) · S^a,

where S is a spin-½ impurity operator and J^a_{m m'} is a (possibly anisotropic) exchange coupling matrix in lead-flavor space. Assume the tunneling exchange couplings (the off-diagonal entries J^a_{12} = J^a_{21}) are weak.

Determine the following:

(a) The physical Bethe-ansatz quasiparticle excitations of this two-flavor Kondo-type model with bias, including their dispersion, statistics, and the flavor/spin/charge quantum numbers they carry.

(b) The bulk two-particle scattering matrix between these quasiparticle excitations in the homogeneous (no impurity) system.

(c) The single-particle impurity scattering matrix describing scattering of these quasiparticles off the impurity spin at x = 0.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has developed nonequilibrium Bethe-ansatz / scattering-Bethe-ansatz frameworks for two-lead and multichannel Kondo impurity problems (e.g. Mehta–Andrei scattering Bethe ansatz, work by Schiller–Hershfield at the Toulouse point, and bosonization-debosonization analyses of the two-lead Kondo problem). These works exhibit physical excitations and bulk/impurity S-matrices at special (e.g. Toulouse) points and for the isotropic multichannel model in equilibrium, but a complete identification of the physical excitations and bulk plus impurity scattering matrices for the generic anisotropic two-lead Kondo tunneling Hamiltonian with arbitrary bias remains incomplete. The problem is therefore best characterized as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Nonequilibrium transport in quantum impurity models: the Bethe ansatz for open systems
status_evidence.snippet: A generalization of the equilibrium Bethe ansatz—the nonequilibrium Bethe ansatz—explicitly constructs scattering eigenstates for the interacting resonance level model and derives exact, nonperturbative results for the steady-state properties.
status_evidence.claim: A nonequilibrium Bethe-ansatz framework constructing scattering eigenstates has been developed for related impurity models.

status_evidence.title: Scattering Bethe Ansatz approach
status_evidence.snippet: Scattering Bethe ansatz approach for nonequilibrium quantum impurity problems.
status_evidence.claim: Scattering Bethe-ansatz approaches to impurity problems out of equilibrium have been formulated.

status_evidence.title: Consistent bosonization-debosonization II: The two-lead Kondo problem
status_evidence.snippet: Two-lead Kondo problem and the fate of its non-equilibrium Toulouse point.
status_evidence.claim: The two-lead Kondo problem has been analyzed at special (Toulouse) points but the general nonequilibrium solution remains delicate.

status_evidence.title: Fermi and Non-Fermi behavior in the anisotropic Multichannel Kondo Model – Bethe Ansatz solution
status_evidence.snippet: Bethe-ansatz solution of the anisotropic multichannel Kondo model.
status_evidence.claim: Equilibrium Bethe-ansatz solutions of related multichannel Kondo models are known, providing partial answers.
